title: hay / había (there is, there was), alguien, uncertain existence → mood tense, tiene que haber

cards.title: hay = there is / there are
cards.body: One word, from haber, that never changes. Alguien = somebody.

examples.en: There's someone here who wants to talk to you.
examples.es: Hay alguien aquí que quiere hablar con usted.

cards.title: Unknown whether it exists → mood tense
cards.body: When asking whether someone or something exists, describe it with the mood tense. When stating what exists, use the normal tense.

examples.en: Is there anyone here who speaks Spanish?
There are two people here who speak Spanish.
examples.es: Hay dos personas aquí que hablan español.

cards.title: había = there was / there were
cards.body: Never 'habían'. 'Spoke Spanish' here describes them as Spanish speakers (ongoing), so the line past fits; hablaron would mean they spoke it at that moment.

examples.en: There were two people here who spoke Spanish.
examples.es: Había dos personas aquí que hablaban español.

cards.title: 'There has to be' = tiene que haber
cards.body: This 'be' means exist, so it's haber, not ser or estar.

examples.en: There must be something you can do.
examples.es: Tiene que haber algo que puedas hacer.

cards.title: The mood tense shows a value system
cards.body: What a language makes you express reveals what it values. The mood tense also varies by dialect and by person. Listen, analyse and enjoy it; don't obsess over getting it right.
